annotation.authors_or_issuer: Haider, A.; Salameh, M.H.; Almethen, W.; Asmara, M.; Warman, A.B.; Husni
key_provisions_or_claims: Sex/companion robots are framed as 'Digital Badal', a permanent technological substitute for the human spouse, threatening the maqasid of marriage.
The necessity (darurah) argument for permitting such robots is rejected as a misdiagnosis that industrialises necessity.
Calls on Muslim states to ban manufacture and sale via sadd al-dhara'i' and siyasah shar'iyyah.
Calls for community education restoring appreciation of human struggle, mercy and patience.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing sex and companion robots in Islamic legal philosophy. It introduces 'Digital Badal' (substitution) as a threat to the purposes of marriage, rejects the necessity-based permission, and urges Muslim states to ban manufacture and sale under sadd al-dhara'i' and siyasah shar'iyyah, together with community education.
annotation.title_clean: Companion Robots, Digital Intimacy and the Purposes of Marriage in Islamic Legal Philosophy
annotation.title_en: Companion Robots, Digital Intimacy and the Purposes of Marriage in Islamic Legal Philosophy
annotation.venue: Malaysian Journal of Syariah and Law
